frontmatter.title: How to Save Spreadsheets Python

blocks.content: Developers using Aspose.Cells in Python need to save or export spreadsheets to specific formats such as XLSX, CSV, or PDF. The `Workbook` class provides methods to persist in-memory spreadsheet data to disk in the desired format.
Aspose.Cells -- Required installation and a loaded document/workbook.
For details on prerequisites, see the Aspose.Cells documentation.

Aspose.Cells provides flexible file saving capabilities for Python developers. The `Workbook` class supports saving spreadsheets in multiple formats including XLSX, CSV, PDF, and others. Developers can specify the output file path and format using the `save()` method, and customize behavior through `SaveOptions` subclasses when needed.

Format selection is determined by the file extension in the output path or by explicitly passing a `SaveFormat` value. Common use cases include saving to XLSX for compatibility with Excel, CSV for data interchange, or PDF for static reporting. When using `SaveOptions`, developers can control settings such as precision, image quality, or worksheet visibility depending on the target format.

Output paths can be absolute or relative, and Aspose.Cells automatically creates parent directories if they do not exist. For integration with existing Python workflows, Aspose.Cells works alongside libraries like `openpyxl` and `pandas`, enabling hybrid processing pipelines where data is prepared using `openpyxl in python` or `openpyxl pandas` patterns before final export.

This section demonstrates how to create a new spreadsheet, write data to a cell, and save it using Aspose.Cells in Python. The example uses the `Workbook` class to initialize a blank workbook, accesses the default worksheet, and writes a value to cell A1 before saving the file in XLSX format.

Aspose.Cells supports saving spreadsheets to multiple formats including XLSX, XLS, CSV, PDF, HTML, and image formats like PNG and TIFF. Format selection is controlled via the `SaveFormat` enumeration when calling the `save()` method on a `Workbook` object.

items: XLSX/XLS: Native Excel formats with full formatting and formula support
CSV: Comma-separated values for data interchange
PDF: Fixed-layout document with optional print optimization
Image formats (PNG, TIFF, etc.): Rasterized worksheet or chart rendering
